clue.text: Neat girl missing hard term in US university

parts.note: neat and trim both mean tidy

indicators.note: missing says the girl's name loses the letter that follows

parts.note: Esther is a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A tidy student skips a difficult semester at an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes H out of ESTHER, leaving ESTER. 'Neat' is not an animal here, just tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: American colleges on a three-term calendar call each academic period by this name.

clue.text: Wicked senior police officer!

definitions.meaning: short for superintendent, a senior rank in British police forces

explanation.definitionFit: Slang praise meaning excellent, and the familiar short form of a superintendent in the British police.

clue.text: Ignorant peacekeepers need energy to contain a conflict

indicators.note: to contain says the first two pieces together hold the last two between them

parts.note: the United Nations, UN, sends peacekeeping forces
E is the physics symbol for energy
a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: Clueless UN troops lack the vigour to stop a fight spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone not informed about a matter is oblivious to it.

clue.text: Eg East Grinstead in relation to its Great Danes?

definitions.text: Eg East Grinstead in relation to its Great Danes?

parts.words: Eg East Grinstead in relation to its Great Danes?
parts.note: the Sussex town's name and the phrase about the dogs use exactly the same letters in a different order, and Eg marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A Sussex town is considered alongside the big dogs living there.
explanation.walkthrough: East Grinstead is a town in Sussex; its thirteen letters can be rearranged to spell 'its Great Danes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by demonstration: the town's letters rearranged spell the phrase about the dogs, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Rich member overcome by booze

indicators.note: overcome by says the member is engulfed, with the drink all around

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A wealthy club member is laid low by drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a rich supply is a plentiful, abundant one.

clue.text: Person who attempts to bring in wrench for European con man

indicators.note: to bring in says a new piece is introduced into the first word
for says the new piece takes the place of the letter named after it

parts.note: to test is to try, so a tester is one who tries
to rick your neck is to wrench or sprain it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to smuggle in a spanner to help a continental swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring in ... for' swaps the first E of TESTER for RICK. Rick is British usage for a sprain, as in ricking your back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both are names for a swindler who cheats by deception.

clue.text: A single politician is unable to keep City free of sin

parts.note: I looks like the numeral one
MP, a Member of Parliament
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district
can't, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: One lone politician cannot keep London's financial district honest.
explanation.walkthrough: The City, capitalised, is London's financial quarter, whose postal district supplies the letters that 'to keep' tucks inside 'is unable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare adjective from Latin meaning not sinning, so blameless.

clue.text: Be jealous of diplomat lacking nothing

indicators.note: lacking says the diplomat's word goes without the letter that follows

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic representative
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Someone resents an ambassador who wants for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes O from ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to covet what another person has.

clue.text: Dagger child brought back without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the turned word goes round the resistance letter
brought back says the word for child is read from right to left

parts.note: kid is an informal word for a child
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A youngster returns a knife and gives no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns KID into DIK, and 'without' (meaning outside) wraps that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the short dagger worn with Highland dress.

clue.text: Specialist transforming clan ethic

indicators.note: transforming says the letters of the two words after it change into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An expert overhauls the moral code of a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforming' rearranges CLAN ETHIC. Specialist is an adjective here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: specialist language is the jargon of a particular field.

clue.text: Heartened about first pair of questions being varied

indicators.note: about says the word for heartened goes round the two picked letters

parts.note: to cheer someone is to hearten them

indicators.note: first pair of takes the opening two letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A quizzer is encouraged that the opening two questions are different.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: such a career or history has had mixed fortunes, good and bad.

clue.text: Old stone prisoner-of-war camp

parts.note: a flag is a flat paving stone

explanation.surface: An ancient camp for captured soldiers, built of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the German name for a wartime camp holding captured officers.

clue.text: Solicit alms on main road going round plant

parts.note: to beg is to ask for charity

indicators.note: going round says the road's name turns about to face the other way

parts.note: the A1, Britain's main road from London to Edinburgh, written with I for the numeral

explanation.surface: A beggar works the high street beside a factory on the bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: The main road is the trunk route from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write its numeral as the letter I, and 'going round' turns the pair about.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a popular flowering species for gardens and pots.

clue.text: A northern lass dipping into books about fruit

indicators.note: dipping into says the three pieces before it plunge inside the turned books
about says the books abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
gel is an affected upper-class pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: A girl from the north browses volumes on oranges and lemons.
explanation.walkthrough: The lass is 'girl' as said in old-fashioned posh British speech. 'about' turns the Old Testament's abbreviation before 'dipping into' fills it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a citrus cross between a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Drink that's part of meal at tearoom

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A beverage comes with the set lunch at a café.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a milky coffee, one kind of beverage.

clue.text: A woman's element, the dried plant collection

parts.note: her is the possessive for something belonging to a woman
barium is the chemical element with symbol Ba

explanation.surface: A lady botanist is happiest among her pressed flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' in the surface means a natural habitat; here it is a chemical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical name for a set of pressed, preserved specimens kept for study.

clue.text: Big wave from Eliot initially, meeting a friend in Paris

parts.note: the poet Thomas Stearns Eliot is known by his initials, T S
the French for a friend is un ami

explanation.surface: The poet gives a hearty greeting on meeting a French pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' asks for French: 'a friend' is UN AMI. The wave looks like a hand gesture but is water.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea surge set off by an undersea earthquake.

clue.text: The girl's a duck, some say

indicators.note: some say tells you the duck's name is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck, source of eiderdown

explanation.surface: Gossips call a young woman a darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' asks for a word pronounced like EIDER, the sea duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female first name.

clue.text: Slowly disappear, seeing Welshman outside English church

indicators.note: outside says the Welsh surname goes round the letter for English

parts.note: Evans is a typically Welsh surname
CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man from Wales fades from view outside an Anglican chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the surname round the English letter only; the church follows afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fade gradually out of sight like vapour.

clue.text: River invading portable shelter, one rising in Staffs

indicators.note: invading says the river's letter pushes its way inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter you carry and pitch
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Floodwater pours into a camper's canvas in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invading' puts R inside TENT. 'one' refers back to River; Staffs is Staffordshire, the English county where this river has its source.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an English river whose source is on Biddulph Moor in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Practical about girl's muscular spasm

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a memo heading
Ali is a short form of Alison, and the possessive adds S
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A hands-on account of a young woman's twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe a sensible, down-to-earth outlook.

clue.text: Electrician finally fixes lights around recreational area

indicators.note: around says the two picked letters go either side of the recreational area
finally takes the closing letter of each of the two words after it

parts.note: a park is a public space for leisure

explanation.surface: A tradesman at last repairs the lamps round the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the S of 'fixes' and of 'lights'; 'around' sets them either side of PARK.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang nickname for someone in this trade, especially on a ship or film set.

clue.text: Ascetic pair in a cult novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters before it take a new order

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An austere couple feature in a book with a devoted following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges PAIR IN A CULT; it is not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: strictly self-denying and austere in morals.

clue.text: Damage lines after engineers form new union

indicators.note: after says the damage and lines follow the engineers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to mar is to spoil or damage
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on lines

explanation.surface: After sabotaging the track, rail workers set up a fresh trade body.
explanation.walkthrough: The union is a marriage, not a trade body. 'after' sends damage and lines behind the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical paraphrase: to wed again is to enter a fresh marriage.

clue.text: Daily crew covering front of wood: it stops leaves blowing about

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper, a paper

indicators.note: front of takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oars

explanation.surface: Each day a gang sheets over the edge of the copse to keep the foliage still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' takes W from 'wood' and 'covering' puts EIGHT round it. The leaves are sheets on a desk, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a heavy desk object that holds loose sheets down in a draught.

clue.text: Consequences of a fine spell at hospital

parts.note: F is the pencil grade abbreviation for fine
a term is a spell or period of time
H is the road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: The results of a pleasant stay on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: what follows on from an event, especially a bad one.

clue.text: New treatment for a minion's sleeplessness

indicators.note: New treatment for says the letters after it are handled afresh and reordered

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: A fresh remedy for an underling who lies awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New treatment for' rearranges A MINIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical name for a habitual inability to get to sleep.

clue.text: Lake frozen over, remain inside? A sound measure!

indicators.note: inside says the word for remain sits within the turned letters
over says the two pieces before it are turned, as one run, to read the other way

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
iced means frozen over
to be is to remain, as in let it be

explanation.surface: With the mere iced up, staying indoors is a sensible step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' means noise, not sensible. 'over' turns lake and frozen together as one run before 'inside' applies.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit used to express the loudness of noise.

clue.text: The Continental newlywed's space for supporters

parts.note: le is the French word for the
a groom is a man just married

explanation.surface: A European hotel sets aside the bride's room for her fans.
explanation.walkthrough: The supporters are your lower limbs, which hold you up, not fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: the room in front of a seat for the limbs that hold you up.

clue.text: Head off like horse chewing top of cultivated shrub

indicators.note: chewing says the horsey word has the picked letter in its mouth, held inside
Head off says the word for like a horse loses its opening letter

parts.note: equine means of or like a horse

indicators.note: top of takes the opening letter of the next word, apt in a down clue

explanation.surface: A pony stretches forward to nibble the tip of a garden bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' cuts the first E from EQUINE, leaving QUINE; 'top of' takes C from 'cultivated', and 'chewing' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hard-fruited bush or small tree, with ornamental flowering kinds too.

clue.text: Discourage grass springing up around town's entrance

indicators.note: around says the turned grass goes round the picked letter
springing up says the grass is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground

indicators.note: entrance, the way in, takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop weeds sprouting round the gateway to the village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'springing up' turns REED into DEER; 'entrance' takes T from 'town's', and 'around' wraps DEER round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to put someone off doing something.

clue.text: Saint's bones, possibly, abandoned by Roman Catholic priest

indicators.note: abandoned by says the Church's two letters leave the longer word

parts.note: a saint's bones kept for veneration are one example of a relic

explanation.surface: A cleric of Rome walks away from holy remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' takes R and C, the first and last letters, off RELIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Old Testament high priest who raised Samuel, crosswords' stock holder of the office.
